patch_description: The bottleneck in this configuration is typically a tight cluster of 3-4 points whose small triangles bind simultaneously; single-point moves cannot always relieve such pair-traps because moving either point alone decreases some other triangle. We add a pair-move search: identify the two points involved in the smallest-area triangles and try moving them together along shared directions (same direction and opposite directions), each candidate fully projected and evaluated. This is placed in a `_polish` routine called after annealing, plus targeted single-point moves around the bottleneck point. Also cache the best solution across calls and keep the annealing schedule but with slightly more iterations at low temperature. The polish loop repeatedly finds the bottleneck triangle, tries 12 single-point directions for each of its 3 vertices plus 24 pair moves (same/opposite directions for the two extremal vertices of the bottleneck triangle), accepts any improving move, and iterates until no improvement. This directly addresses the correlated-pair trap that plain annealing fails to escape at low temperature.
